note: One row per family, written as it finishes. This lane builds nothing and repairs nothing; a defect is a verdict and a repair assignment, never an edit. Nothing here approves an output, promotes a route or opens a commercial path.

ROUTE_IDENTITY.measured: The question put to this lane was whether this petition states its own statutory ground on its own face. It does, and the ground it states is Minn. Stat. 152.18, reaching Minn. Stat. 609A.02 subd. 1 - not subd. 3. Geometry first: the only drawn mark on packet page 4 is two stroked diagonals, 93.19,661.2 to 99.65,667.61 and 93.19,667.61 to 99.65,661.2, read straight out of the decompressed content stream. Item 9's ballot glyphs, located by pdftotext -bbox and converted from top origin, sit at x 90.4-102.4 with cells at y 658.36-670.31 (box 1), 570.36-582.31 (box 2), 514.36-526.31, 473.56-485.51, 401.56-413.51, 313.56-325.51, 225.56-237.51 and 135.16-147.11. The mark falls inside box 1 and inside no other; the nearest other cell is 88 points away. Second, what box 1 prints, read at its own x and y rather than in extraction order: 'A criminal case against you for a possession of a controlled substance under Minn. Stat. 152.024, 152.025, or 152.027 has been dismissed and the proceedings have been discharged under Minn. Stat. 152.18. [Use Order Concerning Sealing/Expunging of Record - Minn. Stat. 609A.02, subd. 1 or 2 (court form EXP106).]' The words 152.024 (yMin 136.49), 152.18 (yMin 151.69), 609A.02 (yMin 167.69) and EXP106).] (yMin 183.68) all belong to the paragraph whose first line is level with the ticked box. So the elected line names its own statute in print, and names the subdivision and the order form that go with it. A court reading page 4 sees one of eleven grounds elected and that ground carries its citation. Third, a reason for each box that could not be this ground, which is the standard asked for: boxes 3 through 10 each print '[Use Order Concerning Sealing/Expunging of Records - Minn. Stat. 609A.02, subd. 3 (court form EXP105)]' and box 11 prints '[Use Findings of Fact, Conclusions of Law and Order to Seal/Expunge Judicial Records Only (court form EXP107)]'. Neither EXP105 nor EXP107 is in this packet - the four bound components are EXP102, EXP104, EXP106 and FEE102 - so none of those nine can be the ground this packet supports. That leaves box 2, the juvenile-certification ground, which routes to EXP106 as box 1 does and so cannot be separated by the component set. Three things separate it: the tick's measured position, 88 points above box 2's cell; item 10 on page 5, written by the packet, which prints 'Type of offense: Fifth-degree possession of a controlled substance', the 152.025 controlled-substance offence box 1 names and an offence class a juvenile-certification ground does not name; and the route's own identifiers, routeKey obligation:track-only:MN:mn_petition_15218 and routeSelectionId mn-exp102-152-18-discharge. Fourth, corroboration on the face of the order: EXP106 prints 152.18 twice, at page 1 finding 1 first branch ('and was sentenced pursuant to Minn. 152.18', against the second branch's 'following certification or reference to district court for prosecution pursuant to Minn. Stat. 260B.125') and at page 3 paragraph 5 ('seals the record of proceedings under Minn. Stat. 152.18'). Both are the judge's to mark and both are correctly unmarked. Fifth, the guide says it in words: 'On EXP102 item 9 the first box is checked: the box for a controlled-substance case dismissed and discharged under Minn. Stat. 152.18 ... If your case was not discharged under 152.18, this is the wrong packet and you should not file it.' One qualification, recorded rather than resolved: EXP102 item 6 prints a bullet requiring 'The statutory or other legal authority under which you are seeking an expungement' and the packet leaves item 6 blank. That is disclosed - the guide assigns item 6 to the participant as a sworn narrative and tells them it must carry the legal authority - so the ground is stated by election and citation on the ticked line rather than recited in item 6's prose. The petition is not under-differentiated.

EXP102 c98430f1a9c7a6d399b7d01de1ef2eee0df5f0a1a07e89a703b307977d7bf541, EXP104 0e776a93b61f28f38fc6b318a9f59b78de4e0cbec102236364cf59ab061b423c and EXP106 da7080f9c0b0135a79b537545e5448da438b63ae0de5d69c25e2513f1170bd85 in private/source-imports/Nationwide_Recovery_Pool_2026-09-02/LegalEase Minnesota/, and FEE102 b8415cddaa06a9c76cf2c4949aee36efe22e3b0ba98783a74063094150c72da8 at MASTER_LIBRARY_SOURCE_DIR/STATES/MN/04_SUPPORTING_PROCESS/MN__SUPPORT__FEE102__affidavit-to-request-fee-waiver__REV-2024-07__EN.pdf. Two committed records disagree on where these bytes live and I measured against the digest, not the path: MASTER_QUEUE.json declares EXP102, EXP104 and EXP106 under 'private/Nationwide Record Clearing/LegalEase Minnesota/' and FEE102 under 'private/source-imports/rcap-d-source-packs-2026-08-12/D2/STATES/MN/...', and neither path exists in this mount, while source-receipt.json discloses exactly that ('declaredPathsInTheQueueAreStale') and resolves by content digest with substitutionMade false. COMPONENT_SET.measured: Scored against the registry and the manifest and then against the queue, all three of which agree here. MASTER_QUEUE.json, product-wiring.json binding and source-receipt.json each name four packetComponents (certificate-of-service-2, fee-waiver-4, primary-filing-1, proposed-order-3) and the same four instrumentKinds. The delivered canonical.pdf carries EXP102 pages 1-6, EXP104 pages 1-2, EXP106 pages 1-3 and FEE102 pages 1-6, seventeen pages, which I read off the printed footers of the delivered pages, not off the manifest. Each form's delivered page count equals its source pageCount in the receipt. Nothing is missing and nothing is extra.

KNOWN_PREFILLS.measured: The packet makes two selections. Only one is disclosed. The guide's disclosure section, headed 'What this packet already says for you', names the EXP102 item 9 box and nothing else. The second selection is on FEE102 page 1 item 2, a printed 'Choose one:' on an affidavit sworn under penalty of perjury under Minn. Stat. 563.01, where the packet marks the first branch, 'I am including my pleadings with this Affidavit (or I have already filed my pleadings but have not yet paid the filing fee)'. I read the mark out of the page 12 content stream (diagonals 110.08,351.2 to 115.37,356.49 and 110.08,356.49 to 115.37,351.2), located the branch's ballot cell at x 108.00-117.46, y 341.38-366.50 by bbox, and rendered the region to confirm it prints as a marked box. The family's own reports/blanks.json records it as routeElectionsMade entry FEE102 p1-cb-y350-x108 with approvedDisposition ROUTE_ELECTION_MADE, so the builder knew it was making the mark. Neither participant-instructions.md nor filing-instructions.md mentions it anywhere; grepping both guides for FEE102 item 2 turns up only the opposite branch, and it is listed under 'Choices only you can make'. A participant is handed a sworn affidavit carrying an assertion made for them that they are never told about. Every other prefill checks out: the 28 text writes I recovered by diffing the delivered pages against the pinned sources are all captions, item 1 name parts, item 3 date of birth, item 4 address, item 10 offence details and the EXP102 signature-block contact lines, each landing under the caption the source prints for it. The alias trap named in DEFECTS_NO_COUNTER_CAN_SEE.json is absent here: EXP102 item 2, 'List any other legal names or aliases you have been known as', carries no glyph at all, so no legal name is standing in for an alias declaration.

PROTECTED_FIELDS.measured: 67 entries are classified protectedFields and I checked the delivered bytes rather than the classification. Nothing is written into EXP102 item 7's criminal-record table, into items 6, 13 or 16, into the EXP102 signature date or the county and state where signed, into anything on EXP104 below its caption (its only writes are County, Court File Number and the defendant name), into any EXP106 finding, ordering paragraph, agency box or the judicial signature, or into any FEE102 public-assistance, income, marital, dependant, property or expense item. The intersection of the 28 written field ids with the 67 protected blankIds is empty. The two refusals that matter most are honoured on their stated grounds: EXP104 is caption-only so that no Minn. Stat. 358.116 declaration of a mailing that has not happened is created, and FEE102's financial items are left to the participant because the platform holds no financial fact.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.measured: Checked both fixtures. Across all 56 writes (28 canonical, 28 boundary) every write rect lies inside its measured source rule: zero overruns on rect.x >= rule.x0 and rect.x+rect.width <= rule.x1. The boundary fixture is the one that matters, since it carries deliberately long values; its longest, the 94-character 'Fifth-degree possession of a controlled substance, aiding and abetting, continued for dismissal', prints in full and runs x 175.6 to 509.98 inside a rule measured x 173.6 to 540, which I confirmed by reading the individual word bboxes off the delivered boundary bytes rather than trusting the report. Three case-number values too long for their caption rules are refused outright and print as empty, not clipped, on EXP102 p1, EXP104 p1 and EXP106 p1, which is the family's own stated doctrine that a clipped value on a filing is a wrong value and not a shorter one. Both ticks are centred in their own ballot cells with clearance on every side. One report discrepancy worth recording, which is a defect in the builder's report and not in the output: reports/actual-writes.json gives overlayTextReadFromFinalPdfBytes for the boundary EXP102 offence write as '...continued for dismis', 91 characters, while the delivered bytes carry the full 94-character value ending in 'dismissal' at x 509.98. The builder's byte reader loses the tail; the page does not.

SELF_HELP_STOP.measured: Two stops are stated and both are tied to a condition the participant can actually recognise. Wrong-ground stop, participant-instructions.md: 'If your case was not discharged under Minn. Stat. 152.18, this is the wrong packet and you should not file it.' Contested-matter stop, filing-instructions.md: 'If an agency or the prosecuting authority objects, the court sets a contested hearing. Automated assistance ends there and you need a lawyer.' That second stop is anchored to something printed on the delivered face - EXP102 page 1 carries the source's own notice that any objection shall be filed within 60 days - so the participant is told where the automated path ends and why. Neither stop invents a threshold the record does not carry.

FILING_DESTINATION.measured: filing-instructions.md: 'File with the district court administrator in the county where the case was decided. The caption of every form in this packet names that county and that court file number.' I checked that claim against the delivered bytes rather than accepting it: the county and the court file number are written on all four captions (EXP102 p1, EXP104 p1, EXP106 p1, FEE102 p1) and read back as the same values on each. No courthouse street address, no clerk's counter, no e-filing portal and no drop-off practice is asserted anywhere, which is right, because nothing in the committed record for this route carries one.

SERVICE.measured: The recurring Minnesota finding does not recur here; I checked for it specifically. filing-instructions.md says of EXP104: 'It lists the agencies that must be served and the agencies to serve if they are related to your case. Six of them are marked (Required) on the form itself.' I counted the printed markers on the delivered page by position rather than by extraction order: exactly six '(Required)' tokens, at x 74.76 y 405.52, 496.01, 576.28 and 685.35 in the left column and x 259.20 y 414.40 and 504.99 in the middle column, which map to boxes 1 MN Bureau of Criminal Apprehension, 2 Office of the MN Attorney General, 3 MN Dept. of Corrections, 4 County Attorney's Office, 5 County Dept. of Corrections (Probation) and 6 County Sheriff's Office. The remaining nine boxes print '(check box & use if related to your case)'. Six stated, six printed. The guide names no box individually, so it calls no conditional box required and it does not describe the County Attorney's Office as discretionary. EXP104 itself is delivered blank below its caption with the reason stated: it asserts under Minn. Stat. 358.116 that service HAS happened, so 'Complete EXP104 after you mail, not before, and then file it with the court.' The guide declines to state a service deadline or method on the ground that the committed record carries none, which is honest; the form's own face carries the method (mailing true and correct copies with sufficient postage in the U.S. Mail) and the participant reads that on the page. Nothing about service is fabricated. Scored PASS on service content; the unnamed Judicial District rule in EXP104's caption is scored under REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING rather than here.

REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.measured: Ten items are classified required-before-filing and each is named in participant-instructions.md with what to supply, and four more are correctly assigned to the court as later completion (hearing date, time, courtroom, remote credentials). Against that, two blanks the filing needs are left with no disposition and no mention. First and worse: EXP104 page 1 draws a rule at x0 418.56 to x1 534.96, baselineY 690.24, whose printed caption is 'Judicial District' - the family's own field census carries it as p1-y690.24-x418.56 with writable true. Nothing writes it, it is in none of the six disposition sets in reports/blanks.json, and neither guide mentions it; the id appears exactly once in the whole family directory, in the census. The same Judicial District blank on the other three forms is classified requiredBeforeFiling and the guide tells the participant to look the district up on mncourts.gov. So the participant is instructed to complete that field on three of four forms and left with a blank one on the proof of service they must sign and file. filing-instructions.md makes it worse by asserting 'This packet leaves EXP104 entirely blank below its caption, and that is deliberate' - which tells the reader the caption is complete when it is not. Second: FEE102 page 1 draws a 179-point rule beside its printed 'Case Type:' (census p1-y637.38-x361.02), left blank, undispositioned and unnamed, even though the guide applies exactly the parallel reasoning to FEE102's Plaintiff/Petitioner line, 'FEE102 is the general civil fee-waiver form and prints no party, while the three court forms in this packet all print State of Minnesota over Plaintiff on their own faces', and even though EXP102, EXP104 and EXP106 all print 'Case Type: Criminal' preprinted. The same reasoning was available and was not applied.

ARTIFACTS.measured: Recomputed sha256 over the delivered fixtures: canonical.pdf cbdea2b8edd3e7151fc376273ac59832c2dbbb0486ad04b7cb08073fce5b3346, which equals both reports/rendered-artifacts.json and the acceptance receipt's boundToCanonicalSha256 in product-wiring.json, so the admitted RASTER_PASS is bound to the bytes I read; boundary.pdf 9ef91d9772ab7307e8877fc52e4db7878b1c4c2a2bf0106d8d63ce10fa7deeda. pdfinfo reports 17 pages, 612x792 letter throughout, no rotation, Form: none, JavaScript: no, not encrypted. Both fixtures, all four report files, the census, the field map, both guides, the receipt, the wiring and the status files are present in the family directory.

PAGE_ORDER.measured: Read the printed footer of each of the 17 delivered pages and took the order from those, not from the manifest: EXP102 Page 1 of 6 through Page 6 of 6 on packet pages 1-6, EXP104 Page 1 of 2 and Page 2 of 2 on 7-8, EXP106 Page 1 of 3 through Page 3 of 3 on 9-11, FEE102 Page 1 of 6 through Page 6 of 6 on 12-17. That is the order rendered-artifacts.json's pageManifest declares and it is the order the packet should file in: petition, proof of service, proposed order, then the confidential fee-waiver affidavit last, which suits the guide's instruction to hand FEE102 to the court administrator separately from the public papers. No page is duplicated, dropped or out of sequence within its form.

ROUTE_OPTIONS.measured: Two option sets, one handled correctly and one not. EXP102 item 9 is correct: I counted the source's ballot CID glyph myself in the decompressed streams, 8 occurrences on packet page 4 and 3 on page 5, so 11 controls; exactly one is marked and the other ten are each enumerated in blanks.notApplicableOnThisRoute with a per-box entry, so nothing is silently dropped. FEE102 item 2 is not. Its printed instruction is 'Choose one:' and it prints two mutually exclusive branches. The packet marks the first branch and records it as ROUTE_ELECTION_MADE, while it classifies the second branch, ballot p1-cb-y266.6-x108, as PARTICIPANT_ELECTION_GENUINE and surfaces it to the participant in the guide's 'Choices only you can make' list as 'I only want to have copy fees waived. I do not have any pleadings to file at this time.' One mutually exclusive set, two contradictory dispositions, and the guide never says the other branch is already marked. A participant who reads their own instructions and marks the branch offered to them files a Minn. Stat. 563.01 affidavit with both branches of a 'Choose one' marked, sworn under penalty of perjury. The two facts are not in tension in the abstract - this packet does include pleadings - but what is delivered invites the participant to contradict it.

REPEATING_ROWS.measured: EXP102 item 7 is the family's only repeating structure: a six-column criminal-record table (Case #, County-State, Type of Charge, Date of Offense, Conviction Yes/No, Date of Conviction) spanning packet page 3. It is measured, and the measurement is that no cell carries an overlay glyph - established by the full source-to-delivered text diff, which shows no added text anywhere on page 3. That is the right answer rather than an omission, and the delivered guide gives the reason on its face: the form demands the participant's whole criminal record from every jurisdiction, the platform holds one matter, and one filled row beside five empty ones would read as a complete record when it is not. Because no row is partly filled, no row misstates. Nothing here resembles the index-versus-printed-row-number defect in DEFECTS_NO_COUNTER_CAN_SEE.json: these binaries carry no AcroForm at all (acroFieldCount 0 in the receipt, Form: none from pdfinfo), so there is no field index that could disagree with a printed row number.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.measured: FEE102, Affidavit to Request Fee Waiver under Minn. Stat. 563.01, is bound as a packet component and delivered at packet pages 12-17. The delivered page 12 prints CONFIDENTIAL at its head and the guide carries the handling rule that follows from it: hand it to the court administrator separately rather than attaching it to the public papers. No filing fee amount is stated anywhere in either guide, and filing-instructions.md says why - 'This packet does not state the amount of the fee, because the amount is set by the court and the committed record for this route does not carry it. Ask the court administrator' - so no number is invented and no statutory waiver is asserted to reach this petition. FEE103 is named as the form the court uses if it wants more detail and is correctly stated to be absent from the packet. The one defect touching FEE102 is its item 2 selection, scored under KNOWN_PREFILLS and ROUTE_OPTIONS rather than here; the waiver instrument itself is present, correctly identified and correctly handled.

I did not read the sibling mn_petition_juvenile_as_adult-set and hold no claim on it; my answer on statutory ground is made from this family's own bytes and records, by election geometry, by the component set (EXP106 present, EXP105 and EXP107 absent), by the packet's own item 10 offence write, and by the route identifiers - none of which requires the sibling.
crossChecks.againstDefectsNoCounterCanSee: Checked all eight deliberately. (1) Field map honest while the finalizer wrote something else - absent; the source-to-delivered diff reproduces exactly the 28 declared writes and EXP102 item 2's alias lines carry no glyph. (2) Blanks binding a participant fact while described otherwise - a variant IS present, at FEE102 item 2, and is scored FAIL. (3) AcroForm index versus printed row number - not applicable, no AcroForm in any of the four binaries. (4) Extracted line order is not column order - guarded against: the six (Required) markers and the eleven item 9 boxes were both located by x and y, not by extraction order. (5) Internal record text printed on a filing - absent; I read EXP106 in full and it is caption-only, with every finding, ordering paragraph, agency box and the judicial signature untouched. (6) A hardcoded zero where a measurement existed - the glyph counts are non-zero (262/42/52/42) and my independent diff matches them. (7) nonWhitespaceGlyphsOutsideMeasuredWriteBoxes reading zero with stray ink present at a widget's own rect - independently defeated: I enumerated every overlay stroke block in all 17 pages, found exactly four, and both marks are ticks inside their own ballot cells. (8) Byte-identical page images across two families - not measured, and not needed for the question asked.
crossChecks.queueVersusReceipt: MASTER_QUEUE.json and source-receipt.json disagree on where the four sources live; both recorded, and I measured against content digest, which is the binding this factory uses and which resolves byte-exact for all four. The queue and the receipt agree on the four components, the four instrument kinds, the four form numbers and the four hashes.

countersHowMeasured.knownRequiredFieldsMissing: 0. The platform holds six facts about this participant (name, date of birth, street address, city/state/zip, telephone, criminal case number). I decoded every flattened appearance stream in the delivered canonical.pdf and each of the six is written on every form that carries a widget for it: seven writes on CIV_EXP_02_A (the six plus the petitioner's name again in the inline blank of the section 4374 sentence), five on CIV_EXP_04_A (which prints no criminal-case-number widget of its own, only the court-assigned Civil Action No.), and six on the composed cover sheet. Nothing the platform holds is left out.

ROUTE_IDENTITY.measured: The route is discretionary Superior Court expungement under 11 Del. C. § 4374 and the packet states it on its own face. CIV_EXP_02_A prints the operative sentence 'Pursuant to 11 Del. C. § 4374, ______ (Petitioner), hereby petitions Superior Court for expungement of the following case(s)' and the build writes the petitioner's name into that very inline widget (field rect [175.0, 532.2, 373.1, 544.6], delivered text 'Pursuant to 11 Del. C. § 4374, Danielle Rose Hargrove (Petitioner), hereby petitions Superior Court'), so the statutory sentence is completed rather than left hanging. The proposed order recites the same section in its WHEREAS clause and in its ordering paragraphs (§ 4372(e)(1), § 4376(a)). The cover sheet names the route in its heading, with the amendment: 'Petition for Expungement of Adult Record, Superior Court, 11 Del. C. § 4374 / Most recently amended at 85 Del. Laws, c. 142, § 10'. The route key, the track registry entry, the packet-set manifest and the source receipt all key to the same track, and the route is distinguished from its neighbours by what is not here: CIV_EXP_08_A, the Superior Court order granting expungement after a pardon, is present in the same custody directory and is not bound by this family, and the guide says in terms that a § 4201(c) felony or a Beau Biden Act offence has the pardon route as its only path. A reader of these three pages can tell which Delaware route is being invoked.

SOURCE_IDENTITY.measured: This was the question put to this lane and the answer is that the receipt binds the official encrypted binaries, not a review derivative. I recomputed sha256 over the pinned sources in the mounted custody: CIV_EXP_02_A f2820f713b9f8e0fb1c0095886e7184d56fda06eef7f65af014ab48922b7839a at 'LegalEase Delaware/download.aspx.pdf', CIV_EXP_04_A 59c3665bbcbf0d22fcf50d7fd1cd9ca688a3c1e3b8e0bea26434f3a389955940 and CIV_EXP_02_B 39b2dd77619f887236be7ebffebc0fa602a2bb1681b1c0aa0f7e4bf5ba92973c under 'LegalEase Delaware/source-acquisition-2026-09-04/'. All three equal the receipt's documents[].sha256 and all three open as encrypted:True under pikepdf. I then reproduced the build's own decryption on this machine with pikepdf 10.12.0, pikepdf.open(source).save(out, deterministic_id=True), and got 4da3c8988b7c28af8485809b1b62b0b196e6722c11def06248085721b337921c, 73b24f3cd1ad7d3ffada5e58cf9f1a4c68d02985dbb0b341e12103fbea578616 and 8bbb2dc70d4950f79eeb1007673970b1bd11ff1fc9c3e3508eac2e5a21515db5 - bit for bit the derivedSha256 values the receipt's transport block declares. The pattern is reproducible and the bound identity is the official binary. The West Virginia failure does not recur here, and I checked for it directly rather than assuming: the committed review derivative at data/rcap-all50/overlays/rescued-encrypted-pdfs/delaware-download-aspx-rescued.pdf is sha256 bc39abcda95beef0acd46f27b3220fefe26fb4b8eac7989a3ea9f509147c3182, 178625 bytes, which is neither the official binary nor the build's derivative - a third decryption with different producer settings - and nothing in this family binds it. It is at least the same revision: it carries the same 44 terminal field names as the official, with no field only in one, and its page-1 content stream is byte-identical to the official's (8 streams, 68523 bytes, sha 645b29f928692d1c...). So no identity here is satisfied with another document's bytes. One defect recorded rather than acted on: the receipt's documents[].byteLength describes the derivative and not the binary it binds. It gives 178713 for CIV_EXP_02_A whose file is 179445 bytes, 986325 for CIV_EXP_04_A whose file is 987462, and 224339 for CIV_EXP_02_B whose file is 227057 - each is exactly the derivedByteLength from the transport block beside it. The binding for this family is stated as exact SHA-256 and the SHA-256 is right, so the identity holds; the byte length printed next to it belongs to a different file.

COMPONENT_SET.measured: Scored against the registry and the manifest as instructed, and it fails on what the delivered packet says the filing contains. The controlling packet-set manifest (data/record-clearing/legal-design-packet-set-manifests.json, sha256 80b5e071055469b6f1aa84e80accd9e8bcc15e00ed3b7b778ba48a0ff85d8bd7, the hash the guide itself prints) declares four components, the fourth being de_discretionary_superior_court-cover-sheet-4, role cover_sheet, requirement required, outputStrategy custom_pleading, order 4. MASTER_QUEUE.json lists only three packetComponents while its own instrumentKinds carries all four including cover_sheet; product-wiring.json's binding repeats the same three-against-four mismatch. Measured against the manifest, all four are accounted for and the artifact is right. The failure is elsewhere. The same manifest's participantActionRequired[10], kind 'file', requirement required, prescribes: 'Assemble the packet in the prescribed order: petition, proposed order, SBI cover letter, then the certified criminal history dated within 45 days. One original plus one copy.' The delivered guide's step 7 reads: 'Assemble it in the order the committed record prescribes: petition, proposed order, cover sheet, then your certified criminal history dated within 45 days. One original plus one copy.' The third item has been changed from the SBI cover letter - an eligibility document the State Bureau of Identification issues after reviewing the certified criminal history, which the same manifest carries at participantActionRequired[2] - to this build's own composed cover sheet, and the substituted order is attributed to the committed record. The substitution reaches the filed page, not just the guide: the delivered cover sheet at packet page 3 prints 'DOCUMENTS IN THIS FILING, IN ORDER / 1. CIV_EXP_02_A ... / 2. CIV_EXP_04_A ..., proposed order. / 3. This cover sheet.' and then 'ATTACHED BY THE PETITIONER / Certified criminal history, dated within 45 days.' - a three-item enumeration of the filing with no SBI cover letter in it, handed to a Prothonotary clerk whose published instruction says the front desk will review the packet 'to ensure it is filled out completely, and in its entirety.' The court's own published instruction agrees with the manifest and not with the packet: CIV_EXP_07_A (Updated 10/4/2024), which this manifest cites as the authority for its own $75 fee, lists the filing order in both its in-person and by-mail branches as 1. Petition, 2. Proposed Order, 3. SBI's Cover Letter, 4. Certified Criminal History. I record rather than resolve the underlying conflict, which is inside one record: the manifest's components array declares a required cover_sheet at order 4 while the manifest's own file action prescribes an assembly containing no cover sheet and an SBI cover letter instead. The build reconciled that conflict silently and printed the result on a participant-facing page as the record's own instruction. Second limb, on the same obligation: the track registry carries an open release blocker whose affectedElement is packet_components - 'Which proposed order the petitioner is expected to lodge. All five Superior Court orders are published as court forms, and the instructions simply say "Proposed Order." Confirm with the Prothonotary whether CIV_EXP_04_A is the one to lodge.' The guide discloses one of the registry's three release blockers, the Cornette partial-expungement question, and not this one, although this one is about the identity of the document in the reader's hand.

KNOWN_PREFILLS.measured: Eighteen values are prefilled and every one is an identity fact the platform holds. I did not take that from the report: I extracted the delivered pages, extracted the two decrypted sources, and diffed them, and the diff yields exactly seven added items on the petition and five on the order, matching the officialInkAudits addedTextItems of 7 and 5; the remaining six are on the composed cover sheet, which has no source to diff against and which I read in full. Then I decoded the text operand of all 80 flattened appearance streams and confirmed each value sits in the widget whose caption it belongs to. No prefill asserts a legal conclusion, an eligibility finding, a disposition, a charge or a date of offence. The charge tables on both forms are entirely unwritten, which the guide states twice and explains from the record: 'The committed record directs that this packet be generated without collecting or reviewing your certified criminal history, and that LegalEase must not represent that it confirmed charge-level eligibility', which I verified against the track registry's packetInstructions, 'LegalEase must not represent that it confirmed charge-level eligibility' and 'Generate the court packet without collecting or reviewing the certified SBI history.' The alias-style defect in DEFECTS_NO_COUNTER_CAN_SEE.json is absent: no field is filled with a value that stands for something broader than itself, and the one field whose name is a run-on sentence ('expungement of the following cases and the charge or set of charges...') is the inline blank in the § 4374 sentence, correctly filled with the petitioner's name and with nothing else.

PROTECTED_FIELDS.measured: 24 blanks are classified protected and I checked the delivered bytes rather than the classification, decoding every flattened appearance on both pages of both fixtures. Every protected blank is empty on the delivered page: the six Attorney General county boxes, both PO Box lines, the Civil Petition No. and the order's 'Leave Blank - Court will assign', both attorney blocks, both language lines and all four interpreter buttons, the manifest-injustice checkbox, the jurat's 'day of' and its two unnamed lines, and the order's paragraph 5 'Other' and its DATE. The reasons given are sound and traceable: the county boxes are a venue election keyed to the participant's own case history, the attorney blocks are refused because the platform holds no representation fact, the Civil Action No. is court-assigned and the order form prints '(Leave Blank - Court will assign)' beside it on its own face, and the judicial officer's signature and date are the judge's. No protected value is asserted anywhere. Three of these fields carry a build-generated empty appearance stream, which asserts nothing and is counted under invisibleWrites rather than here.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.measured: Measured with real font metrics and then confirmed by eye. Each flattened appearance carries its own clip box (a '1 1 m ... W n' path inset one point from the widget rect), so an over-long value would be silently cut rather than spilled, which makes this the obligation most worth measuring directly. I computed each delivered value's printed width from the standard Helvetica AFM advance widths at the size the appearance actually declares. Canonical: every value fits with room, the widest being the petitioner's name at 11 pt needing 121.0 points of 217.1 available. Boundary, which carries the long values: the finalizer shrinks rather than clips, to 9.5 pt for the name and telephone on the petition, 8.36 pt for the inline name, 7.5 pt for the name on the order, and wraps the 44-character street address onto two lines inside a 25.9-point-tall rect. The tightest case is the name on the order at 7.5 pt, needing 164.62 points of 165.90 available. Nothing exceeds its clip box anywhere in either fixture, so nothing is cut. I rendered the canonical page 1 caption and the boundary page 2 caption at 130 dpi and looked at both: values sit on their own baselines, the wrapped address stays inside its cell, nothing overlaps the court's own rules or captions, and no flattening chrome is drawn that the published form does not already print.

SELF_HELP_STOP.measured: The builder invented one stop and flagged it as its own, and this lane was asked to decide whether that is sound. It is, and the reasoning is worth recording. First, which stop is invented: the track registry lists fourteen selfHelpStopConditions and the guide's 'When to stop and get help' section carries fourteen bullets, of which thirteen map onto the registry (two registry entries about pending charges and about serving a sentence are merged into one bullet) and exactly one has no counterpart there - 'You have more than four charges to list. The petition has a published continuation sheet and the proposed order does not.' It is repeated operationally at step 3 of 'What you do, in order'. Second, its factual predicate, which I verified from the official bytes rather than the builder's account: CIV_EXP_02_A's charge table has four printed rows (Row1-Row4 at descending y, five columns each); CIV_EXP_04_A's has four printed rows likewise; CIV_EXP_02_B carries twenty-six rows across 136 terminal fields and its official title is 'Expungement Petition Form Additional Charges Extension Sheet', a petition extension; and no order continuation exists anywhere in the Delaware custody, which holds CIV_EXP_02_A, 02_B, 04_A, 06_A, 07_A and 08_A, the last being the after-pardon order and not a continuation. Delaware's own published instruction CIV_EXP_07_A never mentions more than four charges and never mentions CIV_EXP_02_B at all. So above four charges the packet would carry a complete list on the petition and an order that cannot hold it, and a participant filing that would be asking the court to sign an order covering fewer charges than they petitioned to expunge. The predicate is true. Third, the judgment. A packet inventing a self-help stop is sound where three things hold, and all three hold here. Its factual predicate is verifiable on the delivered documents themselves, so a reader can check it rather than take it. It is stated as the packet's own limit with its reason on its face - 'the petition has a published continuation sheet (CIV_EXP_02_B) and the proposed order does not' - and is not dressed as law, as a court's practice or as the committed record's instruction, in a guide that is otherwise scrupulous about attribution wherever attribution exists. And it errs toward refusing rather than toward delivering: the controlling manifest declares the continuation a supported conditional component precisely for 'When charges exceed the table on the petition', so the stop is narrower than the record allows, not broader. Inventing a stop is a different act from inventing a fee, a deadline, a service rule, a signature or a notarization: those assert facts about the world the packet does not know, whereas a stop asserts only that the packet declines to go further, which is always within its own competence to state. Two qualifications recorded inside this PASS. The invented bullet sits in the same undifferentiated list as thirteen sourced legal-eligibility conditions, so a reader cannot tell that one of the fourteen is a limit of this packet rather than a feature of Delaware law. And the section is headed 'When to stop and get help' without saying anywhere what help means or where to get it, which the Minnesota family in this same shift does state ('you need a lawyer').

FILING_DESTINATION.measured: The guide states: 'The Superior Court for the county where your most recent case was terminated. The committed record is explicit that venue keys to the most recent termination and not to the county of each conviction.' I read the track registry's own venue field and it says 'Superior Court for the county where the most recent case was terminated. Venue keys to the most recent termination, not the county of each conviction.' The guide is faithful to it. The filing mechanics are equally traceable: 'File in person at the Prothonotary with the petition unsigned and identification, signing before the notary, or by mail with the petition already notarized' matches the manifest's notarize and file actions and matches CIV_EXP_07_A sections 4 and 5 on the court's own face. No courthouse address, e-filing portal or clerk's counter practice is invented; the guide names the office and no more.

SERVICE.measured: Every service statement traces to a record or to the delivered form and none is invented. 'You serve the Attorney General, who may object or answer within 120 days. If the Attorney General opposes, you have 30 days to file a response' matches the manifest's serve_party action word for word in substance and matches CIV_EXP_07_A section 6b and 6d on the court's own face. 'The expungement clerk emails a copy of the filing to the Attorney General once a case number is assigned' matches CIV_EXP_07_A sections 4g and 5f. 'The Attorney General contacts the victim under § 9414(a) and reports the victim's position in the answer' matches the receipt's statutory authority list, which carries 11 Del. C. § 9414(a). And the guide's claim that the petition's own pre-printed block is the service list is verifiable on the delivered page: CIV_EXP_02_A prints the Attorney General's three county offices with full street addresses at its head, and the packet writes nothing into that block and alters nothing in it, which I confirmed by the delivered-versus-source content stream comparison. No service deadline, method or recipient is stated that the record or the form does not carry.

REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.measured: The eight requiredBeforeFiling strings the manifest declares are reproduced in the guide verbatim - I compared each of the eight against the delivered participant-instructions.md as an exact substring and all eight are present, and the guide names the record and prints its SHA-256, which I recomputed and which matches. The 44 requiredBeforeFiling blanks are each given a 'what to write' line naming the printed row and the source to take it from. That is the good part. The failure is one blank that the filing needs and that no part of the packet asks the participant for. CIV_EXP_02_A prints in bold 'The following information MUST be completed for the Court to consider the petition' and directly beneath it a checkbox reading 'The continued existence and possible dissemination of criminal records relating to Petitioner causes, or may cause, circumstances which constitute a manifest injustice to the Petitioner.' That checkbox is the petition's operative assertion on the only test this discretionary route turns on. The packet leaves it unmarked, correctly, and classifies it as a protected blank with the right reason - a sworn assertion the participant must make. It then never tells the participant to make it. I mapped all 24 protected blanks onto the nine bullets of 'Things the platform deliberately left blank': the county boxes, PO Box lines, civil action numbers, attorney blocks, interpreter elections and language lines, the signature and jurat, and the order's paragraph 5 and judicial signature account for 23 of them, and this checkbox is the one left over. The guide's step 4 says 'Write your explanation of how the continued existence and possible dissemination of this record harms you on the four ruled lines' and stops there; step 5 names the county box and the interpreter election and not this one; the 'items you must supply' table lists the four ruled lines and not the box; and 'Manifest-injustice explanation - Petition CIV_EXP_02_A, manifest-injustice section' in the requiredBeforeFiling list is those same four lines. A participant who follows this guide exactly writes four lines of explanation and files with the MUST box unticked.

ARTIFACTS.measured: Recomputed sha256 over the delivered fixtures: canonical.pdf b4a52fd021617f602e56a23b9f140828ac704283539c2e9a714fa37ca42629dc, which equals reports/rendered-artifacts.json and equals the acceptance receipt's boundToCanonicalSha256 in product-wiring.json, so the admitted RASTER_PASS is bound to the bytes I read; boundary.pdf 7ecd449c87303093e2f8f60d2c78cfb0ee84224c5112fa16c6c9507886576179. pdfinfo reports 3 pages, letter, Form: none, JavaScript: no, not encrypted, and pikepdf confirms no /AcroForm in the Root and zero annotations on any page, so the AcroForm forms are genuinely flattened and no live widget ships. The fidelity of the flattening is measurable and holds: all 8 of CIV_EXP_02_A's page content streams and all 8 of CIV_EXP_04_A's are reproduced byte-identical in the delivered pages, with the build's additions confined to three appended streams per page that invoke the flattened widget XObjects. The official form is delivered exactly as the Court publishes it.

PAGE_ORDER.measured: Three pages: CIV_EXP_02_A the petition, CIV_EXP_04_A the proposed order, then the composed cover sheet. I read that order off the delivered pages themselves - the petition's own footer prints 'CIV_EXP_02_A Updated 6/12/2024' and the order's 'CIV_EXP_04_A Updated 05/29/2024' - and it matches the pageManifest and the manifest's component order fields (1, 3, 4, with the conditional continuation at 2 correctly absent). The cover sheet's own printed enumeration of the filing agrees with the physical order of the pages it sits behind. Within the artifact the order is right; the defect in what the guide and the cover sheet say the assembled filing should contain is scored under COMPONENT_SET, not here.

ROUTE_OPTIONS.measured: Three option sets and all are handled correctly. The Attorney General county election appears as three buttons on each form; all six are unmarked in the delivered bytes, which I confirmed by decoding each button's flattened appearance, and the guide gives the reason twice, at 'This packet leaves all three unmarked, because which one is yours is a fact about your own case history and not a choice this route makes' and again at step 5 tying it to the venue rule, 'the county where your most recent case was terminated'. The interpreter election is a Yes/No pair on each form with a language line beside it; all four buttons and both lines are empty and both are disclosed. No option is elected by the packet on either form, which is right for a route whose venue and interpreter needs are facts about the participant. Nothing is dropped: I enumerated the button widgets from the sources myself (three county buttons plus Yes and No on each form, and the manifest-injustice checkbox on the petition) and every one is accounted for in the dispositions.

REPEATING_ROWS.measured: Two repeating tables, both four printed rows of five columns, and both entirely unwritten. That is the correct answer and not an omission: the track registry classifies the history-dependent fields as items the participant completes and instructs that the packet be generated without collecting or reviewing the certified history, so a partly filled charge table would be a half-completed sworn list. Because no cell is written, no row is partial and no charge lands on another charge's line. I checked the two defects that hide in tables like these. Row identity: the printed row order matches the field-name digits, resolved from the widgets' own rectangles - petition rows at y 476.4, 461.4, 446.5, 431.6 and order rows at 414.4, 402.4, 390.4, 378.2, both descending. Column identity: resolved by x-position against the printed headings, and both agree. The guide additionally warns that the two tables do not run the same columns - the petition's fourth is Disposition Date and fifth Disposition, the order's fourth is Disposition and Disposition Date and fifth is Court - and that is true of the widget geometry, which matters because a participant copying across without reading would misalign two columns.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.measured: The fee is stated as '$75, per CIV_EXP_07_A', set by the courts under § 4374(j), reproduced verbatim from the manifest's pay_fee action, and it is corroborated on the court's own face: CIV_EXP_07_A prints '$75.00 filing fee' for the Superior Court discretionary route in both its in-person and by-mail branches. The waiver is stated as conditional and quoted from the manifest's apply_fee_waiver action: under § 4372(l), where an outstanding fine or fee is unpaid for reasons other than wilful noncompliance and the person is otherwise eligible, the court may grant the expungement and waive the fines or fees or convert them to a civil judgment, and the guide adds that the entry is conditional and applies only where the participant cannot pay. No fee amount, waiver form or in forma pauperis path is invented, and the guide correctly routes the participant to ask about the § 4372(l) waiver rather than asserting entitlement to it. The separate $72 IdentoGo cost of the certified criminal history is stated as about $72 and attributed to the manifest, which matches CIV_EXP_07_A's own '$72 fee to obtain criminal history (or could be a little more depending on where you choose to have it done)'.

crossChecks.againstClonedFamilyPackets: CLONED_FAMILY_PACKETS.json carries no entry for de_discretionary_superior_court-set. The nearest neighbour in the same jurisdiction is the pardon route, whose order CIV_EXP_08_A sits in the same custody directory and is bound by no part of this family, so the two are separated by their proposed orders and not only by their captions.
crossChecks.againstDefectsNoCounterCanSee: Checked all eight. (1) Map honest while the finalizer wrote something else - absent; the delivered-versus-source diff reproduces exactly the twelve official-form writes the audits declare, and I decoded all 80 appearance streams to confirm. (2) AcroForm index versus printed row number - checked directly on both charge tables by resolving rows from widget rectangles; they agree. (3) Extracted line order versus column order - checked directly by x-position on both tables and on the six Attorney General county blocks; they agree.
